title: Lokkhon case
description: One scored case in the Lokkhon bilingual clinical safety benchmark. Two families share this file: privacy cases (axes B, C, D), which assert what a redactor must remove and must keep; and navigation cases (axes A, E), which assert what the deterministic escalation and matching layers must decide. A case that declares a known failure must say so through limitation_class and limitation_note rather than by being quietly excluded, because an undeclared exclusion is how a benchmark flatters itself.

clinicianReview.description: Adjudication by a credentialed reviewer. Only these two roles count; a case reviewed by anyone else is reported as unreviewed.

derivation.description: Present only on mechanically derived cases. Its existence is what keeps derived variants out of the authored headline n: a derived case shares its identifier, clinical text, and authoring judgement with its source and is therefore not independent evidence.

privacyCase.description: Asserts what the redactor must remove from a string and what it must leave intact. Both halves are required: a redactor that removes everything scores perfectly on leakage and destroys the record.

report_group.description: Coarse grouping the release aggregates by, e.g. phone, name_labeled, injection.

must_not_contain.description: Identifier spans that must be absent after redaction. Every surviving span is a false negative and counts against recall whether or not it is disclosed.

must_preserve.description: Benign clinical text that must survive. Every lost span is over-redaction.

known_identifiers.description: Only consulted when uses_known_identifier_api is true.

uses_known_identifier_api.description: True marks a case that supplies identifiers no production call site supplies. Such cases are excluded from headline metrics so recall is not inflated by a path users never exercise.

expected_residual_risk.description: This case is known to leak. The gate stays green; the leak still counts against recall. If it stops leaking the release reports a stale limitation so the disclosure can be retired.

navigationCase.description: Asserts what the deterministic escalation rule and the specialty matcher must decide for one utterance. Expectations are labels a reviewer set, never the system's own output recorded after the fact.

expected_label_basis.description: Where the label came from. 'protocol' means a published clinical rule, not an author's judgement.

expected_emergency.description: Whether this genuinely is an emergency. Distinct from expected_emergency_rule_fires: the gap between them is the recall-first over-trigger the benchmark reports rather than hides.

expected_emergency_rule_fires.description: Whether the deployed rule is expected to fire. May be true while expected_emergency is false; that is a declared over-trigger.

provider_behavior.description: 'bypassed' means the red-flag rule pre-empted the model; 'error' exercises the fail-soft path.

provider_intent.description: A recorded provider response, so specialty matching is scored against a fixed input rather than a fresh generation.
